subject: Encrypted backup key provenance & operator guardianship request
messages:
From: Tom Green <t.green@tythe.com>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-01-12T08:32:00-08:00
Subject: Encrypted backup key provenance and operator separation request

Hi Naomi,

We're preparing our SIG/SOC2 evidence for Q1 and need artifact-level proof for the keys that protect nightly backups stored in your tenant S3. Specifically: 

- Key lineage for the backup-wrap key (wrap key ID: TW-backup-wrap) showing creation, wrapping key (KEK) derivation, and any rotations in the past 12 months.
- HSM operator separation controls and operator identity trace for any HSM ceremonies that touched the KEK.
- KMS access audit trail for the period 2025-12-01 to 2026-01-12 (redacted is OK for user PII) and an example of the exportable audit CSV.
- Transport manifest for the S3 transfer (checksums, wrap metadata) when backup bundles were written.

Can you provide a packaged bundle (zip) containing the items above or point us to a secure transfer? If some items require an executed NDA or DPA, let me know and I'll route it internally.

Thanks,
Tom Green
Security Engineer, Tythe Payments
security@tythe.com

Attachment: (none)

From: Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.com>
To: Tom Green <t.green@tythe.com>
Cc: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-01-12T11:05:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Encrypted backup key provenance and operator separation request

Hi Tom,

Thanks for the clear list — we can deliver a focused bundle that covers lineage, the KMS audit slice you asked for, HSM attestation, and the S3 transport manifest. A few quick notes and next steps: 

1) We have a manifest template that makes it easier for your auditors to parse the wrap metadata; attaching for your review.
2) For full, unredacted KMS operator identities and raw HSM ceremony logs we require an executed NDA. If you can sign the attached DocuSign, we will provide the full logs; redacted samples are fine in the interim.
3) Delivery options:Secure SFTP (we can create a time-limited account + checksum verification) or an encrypted ZIP pushed to the Drive link below. I attached SFTP instructions.

I'll let Marissa add the initial sample files and target timeframe for the complete bundle.

Best,
Naomi Feldman
Senior Security Program Manager
Redwood Inference
naomi_feldman@redwood.com

Attachments: redwood_kms_manifest_template.xlsx (spreadsheet), sftp-instructions.txt (txt)

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Tom Green <t.green@tythe.com>
Cc: Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.com>, Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-01-13T09:14:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Encrypted backup key provenance and operator separation request

Tom —

Looping off the ops side. Per Naomi's note, attaching an initial evidence pack with redacted audit logs and the HSM attestation PDF. High level:

- kms_access_log_2026-01-sample.csv: an export (redacted PII) showing KMS use events for the backup-wrap key; columns include timestamp, key_id, operation, principal, request_id, ip_address (redacted)
- hsm_attestation_2025-11.pdf: HSM vendor attestation for the KEK wrap ceremony dates (vendor-signed), includes public key fingerprints for verification
- backup_wrap_manifest_202601.zip: manifest file and checksums for nightly backups written in January (sample subset)

Notes / caveats: the attached samples are redacted to remove internal operator email addresses and any customer-identifying data. If you need full operator identity traces we can provide them after NDA/DPA acceptance; I included the DocuSign link Naomi referenced in my note below for your legal team. 

Also: The KEK wrapping algorithm is AES-GCM wrap with RSA-OAEP for operator key exchange in our current production profile. The KEK itself underwent a planned rotation on 2025-10-16 (UTC). I can produce the rotation record and the operator ceremony log under NDA.

If you want a short signed attestation letter on algorithm and rotation schedule, we can get that on letterhead; say if that's sufficient for the SIG reviewer.

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
Crypto Operations Lead
Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.com

Attachments: kms_access_log_2026-01-sample.csv (csv), hsm_attestation_2025-11.pdf (pdf), backup_wrap_manifest_202601.zip (zip)

From: Tom Green <t.green@tythe.com>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-01-15T16:04:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Encrypted backup key provenance and operator separation request

Naomi / Marissa —

Confirmed receipt of the sample artifacts, thank you. A couple quick follow-ups before we route to our SIG reviewer: 

- The brief algorithm statement was helpful. Can you confirm whether the KEK (TW-backup-wrap) was rotated again after 2025-10-16? We need confirmation the KEK has not been re-wrapped or re-derived in the last 90 days.
- If you can provide the signed attestation letter stating the algorithm (AES-GCM wrap + RSA-OAEP exchange) and the recorded rotation dates, that will likely meet our first pass.

We're starting legal on the NDA — they'll send the DocuSign this week. Once signed, we'll request the unredacted operator trace and the full ceremony log.

Appreciate the quick turnaround.

Best,
Tom Green
Security Engineer, Tythe Payments
security@tythe.com
